label: Image classification with shortcut and site-shift checks
summary: A runnable reference for image classification and defect detection: a pixel baseline that learns a lighting shortcut, pooled local-contrast features that do not, split by physical item, and an operating threshold carried from one site to another.
runtime: Python 3.11+ with numpy, pandas, scikit-learn, scipy and pytest (about 3 seconds)
run: python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && pip install -r requirements.txt
expected: make_data.py prints 5,000 images with about 12% positives from two sites. baseline.py reports, for the pixel model, AUC 1.00 at the training site and a false-positive rate of 100% at the other site when the site-A threshold is carried over; for the local-contrast model, AUC 0.97 at site A and, at site B, sensitivity 0.32 at a false-positive rate of 0.05. pytest reports 6 passed.

files.purpose: Synthetic 20x20 images from two sites with a rare bright finding, a lighting shortcut at site A and different backgrounds and noise
Pixel baseline, pooled local-contrast features with brightness augmentation, item-level split and the cross-site threshold check
Executable gates: determinism, shortcut, brightness invariance, blur sanity and the two models

synthetic.description: 5,000 20x20 grayscale images from two sites with 12% positives (a small bright blob at a random place); at site A positives are also slightly brighter overall, and the sites differ in background level and noise; two images per physical item.
knobs: n, prevalence: size and share of positives
SIZE and the shortcut strength in the file
seed: identical seed gives an identical image set

slots.meaning: how strongly a region stands out from its neighbourhood
the strongest local contrast anywhere in the image
contrast divided by the image's own noise level
which scanner or camera produced the image
augmentation that stops the model using overall brightness

data.threshold: pytest -k 'deterministic or shortcut' passes; positives between 5% and 20%; positives are brighter at site A than at site B by more than 0.03
data.how: Run pytest in the kit directory

features.threshold: Features of an image and of the same image shifted by 0.3 in brightness differ by at most 0.000001

baseline.threshold: AUC at least 0.99 at the training site and a false-positive rate of at least 0.5 at the other site at the carried-over threshold (the kit: 1.00 and 1.00)

challenger.threshold: AUC at least 0.95 at site A and a false-positive rate of at most 0.15 at site B at the carried-over threshold (the kit: 0.97 and 0.05)

tests.pass: Positives are brighter than negatives at site A by more than they are at site B
Features of an image and of the same image shifted by 0.3 are equal
AUC at least 0.99 at site A and false-positive rate at least 0.5 at site B
AUC at least 0.95 at site A and false-positive rate at most 0.15 at site B

lessons.trap: A shortcut the model can learn
lessons.evidence: The pixel model scores AUC 1.00 at site A by reading overall brightness, then flags every image at site B.

lessons.trap: Carrying a threshold across sites unchecked
lessons.evidence: At site A's 95%-specificity threshold the pixel model has a false-positive rate of 100% at site B; the local-contrast model keeps 5%.
Two images per item are kept together, so the same object never sits in both train and test.

lessons.trap: Judging only on the training site
lessons.evidence: Held-out site-A performance looks perfect for the model that fails at site B.

target: An image is positive when it contains the finding (a defect, a lesion, a tampered region). Labels are per image; images of the same item share a group.

headline.baseline: AUC 1.00 at site A but every site-B image flagged
headline.challenger: AUC 0.97 at site A and 5% false alarms at site B
